gchem-b:GC_s8.w: The boiling point is 100.21°C. The rise is ΔTb = i·Kb·m = (2)(0.52)(0.20) = 0.208°C, which rounds to 0.21°C above pure water.
s: Add the rise to 100.00°C to get 100.21°C.
t: This rise of 0.10°C leaves out i. KCl splits into two ions, so the rise doubles.
A dissolved solute always raises the boiling point, so it cannot stay at 100.00°C.
This uses i × Kb = 1.04 and never multiplies by the 0.20 m concentration.
This adds Kb alone, which is the rise for a 1 m solution of a solute that does not ionize.
c: What would the boiling point be for 0.20 m glucose in the same solvent?
Glucose does not ionize, so i = 1 and the rise is 0.52 × 0.20 = 0.10°C, giving 100.10°C.
